text: Rice can be processed into a range of packaged snack food products for retail sale as a way to add value beyond selling raw grain. Examples shown in the source deck include: plain rice crackers in individual wrapped packs; round rice cookies mixed with what appears to be black sesame seeds and dried herbs, sold in bulk clear bags; small baked rice-flour biscuit-style snacks in printed wrappers (packaging shows Chinese-language branding, suggesting an imported/regional reference example rather than necessarily a Cambodian product); and puffed or expanded rice snack chips (similar to rice crisps/rice cakes) sold in flavored retail bags including a 'cheese' flavor variant.

text: Rice is also cited as a base ingredient or fermentation medium for sauce and seasoning products, shown as small glass or plastic bottles of what appear to be artisanal or small-batch condiments and dark liquid seasonings. The slide does not specify the exact sauce type (e.g., rice vinegar, rice wine sauce, or fermented seasoning), only that 'Sauces and Seasoning' is listed as its own value-added product category derived from rice, packaged for retail sale in small bottles.
